title: Defend: ECC key COPY guard missing — future-proofing gap vs HMAC COPY guard
description:
The WC_ALGO_TYPE_COPY handler guards CIPHER (Aes devCtx), HMAC (Crypto2DevHmacCtx devCtx), and HASH (Crypto2DevHashCtx devCtx) against aliased devCtx on copy. There is no guard for WC_ALGO_TYPE_PK (ecc_key devCtx, which stores a hardware key fd).

Current state: wolfSSL does NOT dispatch wc_CryptoCb_Copy for PK objects. Only SHA-256/384/512 and SHA-3 copy functions call wc_CryptoCb_Copy (confirmed by grep of cryptocb.c callers). So the missing guard does not cause a current bug.

Risk: if wolfSSL upstream adds CryptoCb COPY dispatch for wc_ecc_copy_key (analogous to wc_Sha256Copy), an ecc_key with a hardware key fd in devCtx would have its fd pointer aliased. Whichever copy is freed first closes the fd; the second object then calls ioctl() on a closed (possibly reused) fd.

The HMAC COPY guard has this explicit comment: 'so that if upstream ever adds CryptoCb COPY dispatch for HMAC, the port immediately returns WC_HW_E'. The same reasoning applies to PK. Adding a guard for WC_ALGO_TYPE_PK before the fallthrough CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE return is the consistent fix.
